title: Resolution: clauses and finite refutations
summary: Use one inference rule on clauses, prove refutational completeness by eliminating atoms, and obtain a finite satisfiability procedure.
abstract: If at least one of two switches must be on, but both are required to be off, the requirements cannot all hold. Resolution exposes this contradiction by combining two clauses at a time until no alternative remains. We define its single inference rule and prove that it finds every contradiction in a finite collection of clauses. The proof explains how to forget one atom while preserving exactly the restrictions on the remaining ones. It also gives a terminating procedure for satisfiability and a way to prove a propositional formula by refuting its negation.
